items.title: Friday afternoon: new national numbers are in — flu positivity holds at 14.3%, weekly outbreaks climb to 178, and the Children's Hospital wait is back up to about 4 hours
items.body:
A real update since this morning: the Public Health Agency of Canada refreshed its national respiratory virus report today (Nov 27), with data for the week ending Nov 21. Across Canada, 14.3 per cent of flu tests came back positive — essentially flat from about 14.5 per cent the week before — and flu activity sits at moderate. COVID-19 is at 7.2 per cent of tests positive and increasing, though its activity level is still rated low, and RSV is at just 0.7 per cent of tests positive, stable and very low nationally.

Two national lines worth a parent's eye: PHAC counted 178 respiratory outbreaks in the week, and that number is increasing, and the weekly respiratory hospitalization rate rose to 4.0 per 100,000 people, also increasing. Flu season is not peaking and fading — it is still building as the holidays approach.

Nothing new locally since this morning: Fraser Health's outbreak page is still last updated Nov 26, and its newest declaration is still the Nov 25 influenza outbreak at Cottage and Worthington Pavilion that we covered this morning. BCCDC's Nov 26 weekly summary also still stands: flu moderate in B.C., COVID-19 stepped up to moderate, and RSV still low province-wide in lab testing.

Our live board is unchanged this afternoon: influenza A is High and Stable, everyday cold viruses (entero/rhinovirus) are High and Stable, and RSV is High and Stable. COVID-19 is Medium and Stable, seasonal coronavirus and hMPV are Low but Rising, and parainfluenza, adenovirus and influenza B are all Low. As always, that is our Metro Vancouver snapshot — PHAC and BCCDC's province- and country-wide lab picture calls RSV very low, so read the two as different lenses, not a contradiction.

At the ER door, the wait has climbed again: BC Children's Hospital's posted wait was about 4 hours at our check this afternoon (source updated 3:47 p.m.), up from about 2 hours 45 minutes this morning. Waits swing through the day, so check the live board before heading out. For non-urgent worries, HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide where to go, and for a true emergency, call 911.

Outside, it is a drizzly Friday: 5–10°C, currently about 8°C, with air quality at low risk (AQHI about 2). Flu shots are free in B.C. for everyone 6 months and older, and kids under 9 who have never had one need two doses at least four weeks apart, so starting now still leaves time before the holidays.

items.title: Thursday morning: coastal flood waters peak this morning, flu A and cold viruses stay High, and the Children's Hospital wait is about 5 hours 30 minutes
items.body:
A quick heads-up for families this morning (Nov 26): the coastal flooding risk peaks this morning at about 8:40 a.m., with the highest coastal water levels Vancouver has seen in four years, under an orange warning from Environment and Climate Change Canada. The City of Vancouver plans to close the seawall between Prospect Point and Third Beach, Jericho Pier, and the Southlands shoreline trails today. Please keep children and pets away from the water, and never walk, bike or drive through flood water.

On the illness side, there is no new outbreak news overnight. BC Centre for Disease Control's latest weekly summary still stands: flu at moderate levels across BC, COVID-19 at low-to-moderate, and RSV still low in lab testing.

Our live virus board is unchanged this morning. Influenza A is still High and Stable, tied with everyday cold viruses (entero/rhinovirus), also High. COVID-19 is Medium, and RSV is Medium but Falling. Seasonal coronavirus and hMPV are Low but Rising, and parainfluenza, adenovirus and influenza B are all Low.

At the ER door, BC Children's Hospital's posted wait early this morning was about 5 hours 30 minutes. Waits swing a lot during the day, so check the live wait times on this page before you head out.

Seasonal reminder: with flu A at High, hand washing, fresh air at indoor gatherings, and keeping sick kids home from school and daycare still do most of the work.

items.title: Wednesday afternoon: an orange coastal-flooding warning is in effect for Metro Vancouver — the highest water in four years is expected Thursday morning — and the Children's Hospital wait has climbed to about 5 hours 30 minutes
items.body:
A new weather warning for families today (Nov 25): the City of Vancouver says Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued an Orange Warning for coastal flooding along Metro Vancouver's coastlines, including Vancouver, driven by extremely high tides, storm surge and rainfall over the next several days. The highest risk is Thursday morning, Nov 26, with water levels expected to peak at about 8:40 a.m. — the city says these will be the highest coastal water levels Vancouver has seen in the last four years.

Shorelines along the Fraser River and English Bay, and low-lying areas including Southlands, the South Vancouver Industrial Area and Locarno Beach, are at elevated risk. On Thursday the city plans to close the seawall between Prospect Point and Third Beach, close Jericho Pier, and close the Southlands shoreline trails from Wallace Street to McCleery Golf Course. The city's advice for families: keep children and pets away from the water, and never walk, bike, drive or swim through flood water. Updates are posted through the Alertable app and at vancouver.ca/alerts.

On the illness side, nothing new since this morning: Fraser Health's outbreak page is still last updated Nov 24, and its newest declaration is still the Nov 23 stomach-illness outbreak at Langley Memorial Hospital that we covered this morning. items.title: Friday afternoon: new national flu numbers climb again — nearly 15% of tests positive — B.C. may be near its peak, and the Children's Hospital wait is back up to about 6 hours
items.body:
A real update since this morning: CBC News reported today (Nov 20) on the latest Public Health Agency of Canada figures, covering the week ending Nov 14. Nearly 15 per cent of flu tests across Canada came back positive, up from close to 14 per cent the week before, with outbreaks and hospitalizations also up and influenza A detected in almost all test samples.

Why this matters for families here: the strain circulating most this year is H1N1, which experts say can hit younger adults and children harder than usual. Dr. Bonnie Henry, B.C.'s provincial health officer, told CBC that B.C. has seen emergency room and doctor's office visits go up a lot for young children — particularly ages zero to five, and then young elementary-age children — while adults are not seeing it so much yet. Toronto infectious-diseases specialist Dr. Allison McGeer said B.C. is probably close to the peak of this wave by now, even though Canada-wide the season may still be far from peak, with a possible second surge later in the winter. Henry also said she is hopeful this season will not be as severe as some recent years, because RSV is not circulating heavily at the same time — the latest federal numbers put COVID-19 at more than six per cent of tests positive, and RSV at less than one per cent.

No new local outbreaks to add: Fraser Health's outbreak page is still last updated Nov 18, and the newest declarations are still the ones from Nov 17 — a COVID-19 outbreak at Ridge Meadows Hospital and a flu outbreak at Northcrest Care Centre.

Our live board is unchanged this afternoon: Influenza A is still on top at High and Stable, everyday cold viruses (entero/rhinovirus) are High but Falling, COVID-19 is Medium and Stable, and RSV is Medium and Falling. Influenza B is Low, adenovirus is Low and Rising — the only one still creeping up — and parainfluenza, seasonal coronavirus and hMPV are all Low.

At the ER door, the wait has swung back up: BC Children's Hospital's posted wait was about 6 hours at our check this afternoon, up from about 2 hours 45 minutes this morning. Waits swing through the day, so check the live board before heading out. For non-urgent worries, HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide where to go, and for a true emergency, call 911.

Outside, it is still 4–10°C and overcast, with air quality at low risk (AQHI about 2). The habits that help most right now stay the same: wash hands often, and keep kids home with a fever or a new cough. Experts stress it is still worth getting a flu shot — flu shots are free in B.C. for everyone 6 months and older, and kids under 9 who have never had one need two doses at least four weeks apart, so starting now still leaves time before the holidays.

items.title: Federal data now puts B.C. in the 'high' flu category — and flu outbreaks are hitting Lower Mainland care homes
items.body:
New federal numbers reported today (Nov 13) raise the flag a notch higher than this morning's provincial update. Health Canada says flu activity is rising across the country and is expected to keep trending upward in the coming weeks, with B.C. — along with Alberta, Prince Edward Island and the Yukon — seeing a high percentage of tests coming back positive. The Vancouver Sun, reporting on the same federal data, puts B.C.'s flu test positivity at public health laboratories at 17.8 to 27.4 per cent, with only Nunavut higher.

Why does BCCDC call B.C. flu 'moderate' while the federal scale says 'high'? The two agencies use different yardsticks — PHAC itself notes federal and provincial activity levels are expected to differ. The direction both point to is the same: flu is climbing, and earlier than usual.

You can see it in care homes, too. Fraser Health's outbreak bulletin, last updated Nov 12, lists 12 active influenza outbreaks at long-term care homes across the region, declared between Oct 23 and Nov 10 — plus COVID-19 outbreaks at three hospitals. Fraser Health asks anyone with a cough, fever or flu-like symptoms to please not visit care facilities right now. If your kids have grandparents in care, a sick-day visit can wait — a video call is the safer hello this week.

This afternoon's snapshot from our live board: Influenza A ranks High and Rising, and RSV has moved up to High and Rising as well. The posted ER wait at BC Children's Hospital was about 6 hours 30 minutes at our last check this afternoon, up from about 3 hours 30 minutes this morning — waits swing a lot, so check the live board before heading out. For non-urgent worries, an urgent and primary care centre or HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide; for a true emergency, call 911.

One practical note: flu shots are free in B.C. for everyone 6 months and older, and kids under 9 who have never had a flu shot need two doses, at least four weeks apart — so starting this week still leaves time to get both in before the holidays.

items.title: BCCDC's Nov 12 update: flu is moderate, RSV is still low — but kids' respiratory visits are ticking up
items.body:
BCCDC's newest weekly summary, published Nov 12, says influenza test positivity in BC is at moderate levels, and flu indicators across Canada were moderate and increasing in the most recent reporting week.

RSV is still quiet for now — test positivity remains low and wastewater levels are stable and low — while COVID-19 test positivity is low-to-moderate, wastewater levels are moderate-to-high at most sites, and hospital admissions have stayed low in recent weeks.

One note for parents: BCCDC says emergency department and primary care visits for respiratory illness are still at low levels overall, but there have been recent increases among children.

Today's snapshot from our live board: COVID-19 and Influenza A rank High in our BC wastewater ranking, RSV is marked Rising, and Influenza B is Low; this morning, BC Children's Hospital's posted ER wait was about 3 hours 30 minutes.

A season reminder: flu and COVID vaccines are available in BC at no cost for everyone 6 months and older, and if your child is not in urgent trouble, HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide where to go.

BCCDC's latest weekly summary (Nov 5) puts influenza activity in BC at moderate, and provincial testing suggests flu is picking up earlier than usual this season — most flu detections so far are influenza A (H1N1). COVID-19 activity across BC is low-to-moderate, and RSV is still low for now.

The germ showing up most often in recent BCCDC sentinel swabs is none of those — it's the everyday cold viruses (entero/rhinovirus), ahead of flu. In LittleBuggy's own Metro Vancouver wastewater snapshot, COVID-19 and Influenza A currently rank High, while RSV is Low but rising: the season is warming up, not peaking.

Some calmer news on measles: the Public Health Agency of Canada declared the countrywide measles outbreak over on Oct 19, and BCCDC reports no measles cases in BC since May. Travel-related cases can still appear, so keeping kids' vaccinations up to date still matters. This season's flu and COVID vaccines are now open in BC for everyone 6 months and older, at no cost.

Today's snapshot from our live board: the posted ER wait at BC Children's Hospital this afternoon was about 4 hours. If your child isn't in urgent trouble, an urgent and primary care centre or HealthLink BC at 811 can save you a long night.
